about: The suites of dev/engine-tests. kind: harness (scripts on the production Rhino jar over the mk.* mocks), guard (the event guard on the real KubeJS event classes: guard/GuardChain.java), members (the mocks against the real classes), known-false / truth-fresh (the recorded engine tables), parse (ParseAll), loot (audit_loot.py), rosters (dev/rosters/validate.py), liveness (dev/loud/gen_liveness.js --check). fast = runs in the pre-push hook; ci = needs no mod jar beyond Rhino; snapshot = can record a golden snapshot. In a harness suite an entry is a file of this folder, 'server:<path>' / 'startup:<path>' (a pack script, evaluated directly), {load: [...]} (pack scripts through T_loadAll, so a script that fails to load is a recorded failure), {patch, find, replace} inside a load list (a patched copy), or {js: '...'} (generated; ${server:x.js} becomes the path), or {gen: 'name'} (a file run.py generates: registry-expect = what dev/rosters/rosters.py says of the pack's registries). expect = the exact number of checks.

suites.name: truth-fresh
suites.about: the engine member tables in truth/ were recorded from the KubeJS, Rhino and Architectury jars the pack index names today

suites.name: known-false
suites.about: every name on the known-false list (inv.size, level.gameTime, ...) is still absent on the engine, and its replacement is still there

suites.name: mock-honesty
suites.about: no mock offers a member, a kind of member or an arity that the real class does not have

suites.name: dialect
suites.about: what this Rhino build does with const / let / var, strings from Java, Set and Map: the facts the lints and the scripts rely on

suites.name: mock-facts
suites.about: the mocks give the real engine's answer to every engine fact they answer at all (truth/engine-facts.txt)

suites.name: registry-data
suites.about: dev/rosters/validate.py: every id of kubejs/config/icraft/registry/*.json is something the game registers (dev/registry), the files are consistent, and no boss or dimension deviates from the expectations without a reason in dev/rosters/accepted.json

suites.name: registry
suites.about: kubejs/server_scripts/0_lib_registry.js (icraft.bosses, icraft.dims) answers every id and every system as dev/rosters/rosters.py does; ids are normalised (a Java string works); a registry that cannot be read is an error on every call, never an empty roster; core.isBoss asks it

suites.name: core-helpers
suites.about: the engine-safe helpers of global.icraft.core: idSet answers a Java string, a JS string and a ResourceLocation alike; eachMainSlot walks slots 0-35 of an inventory that has no `size`; playerTier is the highest tier stage held; blockIfLoaded never reads a block of an unloaded chunk; warnOnce and now

suites.name: inventory-scan
suites.about: economy/relic_sink.js on a mock inventory that behaves like the real one: the scan visits slots, the deny list denies, the cap key is stable

suites.name: ascension
suites.about: endgame/ascension.js + scaling/zz_ascension_scaling.js: status and operator commands, the !ascend switch (off), player bonuses, mob scaling

suites.name: ascension-open
suites.about: the same scripts with ASCEND_PLAYER_COMMAND_OPEN switched on in a patched copy: the activation path

suites.name: onboarding-bridge
suites.about: quests/onboarding_bridge.js: the Level Up dummy fires at any aptitude 2+, waits for its dependency, never without a readable capability

scopes.js: var T_BRIDGE = '${server:quests/onboarding_bridge.js}', T_WANT = 2, T_WANT_LOG = 'any aptitude at level 2+'; T_loadAll(['${server:00_icraft_guard.js}', '${server:0_tick_master.js}'])

suites.name: spawn-buff
suites.about: the five scaling scripts + core.spawnBuff against the same scripts as of ffe5cef3 (fixtures/): buffs survive a save/load, a first spawn is bit-identical, legacy mobs are repaired

suites.name: event-guard
suites.about: kubejs/*_scripts/00_icraft_guard.js on KubeJS's REAL handler chain (EventHandlerContainer.handle from the KubeJS jar): a guarded cancel / success / exit reaches KubeJS intact, a throw is reported once and the chain goes on, an engine-level throw is isolated WITH a line and never masks an exit, a java.lang.Error is not isolated; switched off, it behaves like no guard; its three copies are one file. Liveness (icraft.live): a registration is ARMED when made, FIRED once the first time its handler finishes, a cancel counts as fired, a throw is FAILED and not fired; the summary line, NOT ARMED / UNLISTED against an expected list, the digest gen_liveness.js computes

suites.name: liveness
suites.about: ARMED and FIRED outside the guard: a tick function of 0_tick_master.js and a hurt handler of 0_lib_core.js are armed when registered and fired the first time they return (not when they throw, not behind a closed gate); a curated feature (the relic sink and its deny list) fires where it did its work; zzz_icraft_live.js prints the one summary line, compares with kubejs/config/icraft/live/expected.json, collects FIRED lines for a second, and never prints a player name

suites.name: overload-calls
suites.about: overload_calls.py: no script calls a Java method with a value that fits two of its overloads (entity.spawnAtLocation(Item.of(id)) throws 'the choice of Java method is ambiguous' at the call; it kept every first-kill reward from dropping). The risky overload groups come from truth/engine-members.json; each call shape the scripts use carries the verdict of a real full-pack server

suites.name: liveness-manifest
suites.about: dev/loud/gen_liveness.js --check: dev/loud/liveness_manifest.json and kubejs/config/icraft/live/expected.json (x3) are exactly what the scripts register, name and report today; a registration added, renamed or removed without regenerating fails here (needs node, like the script lints)

suites.name: parse
suites.about: every script of the three trees compiles on the real parser (dev/rhino_parse/ParseAll.java)

suites.name: loot
suites.about: dev/audit_loot.py: every loot script on the real Rhino against the recording LootJS mock, joined with the installed jars (needs the whole instance)
